set.body:
Intaglio has no diverging (signed) colour primitive. `Palette.gradient(from, to)` is a two-point linear sRGB interpolation, and the only named ramps are `ColorRamp.Grayscale` and `ColorRamp.Heat` (Display.scala:166-172), both sequential. Signed data — anything centred on zero, which is most statistical imaging — has no supported encoding.

Every consumer therefore hand-rolls one, and they drift. Observed in PLS Neuro, a downstream consumer:

- Its brain overlay built two `ColorRamp`s around a hand-picked neutral and switched on the sign of the value.
- Its contrast plot wrote `t => if t <= 0.5 then Palette.gradient(negative, ivory)(t*2) else Palette.gradient(ivory, positive)((t-0.5)*2)` inline at the call site.
- The two ended up with OPPOSITE sign conventions: rust meant +1 in the overlay and negative in the contrast plot, and the two rusts were dE76 10.2 apart — perceptually the same colour, opposite meaning, both reachable on screen at once. That is a misreading hazard in a scientific tool, and it happened because the library offered no shared primitive to reach for.

REQUESTED
1. A diverging palette constructor taking `negative`, `neutral` and `positive` with a symmetric domain, so a consumer names its endpoints and the library owns the interpolation and the midpoint. Include the `Rgba32` raster form alongside the `Rgba` scene form so overlay and plot cannot diverge.
2. Interpolation through a perceptually uniform space (Oklab) rather than raw sRGB channels. Linear sRGB interpolation through a light neutral produces a non-monotone lightness ramp and muddy mid-tones; for a map whose whole job is conveying magnitude that is a presentation defect, not a taste question.
3. At least one named, colour-vision-safe diverging default. Blue-neutral-rust survives deuteranopia and protanopia; the common red-green diverging pair does not.
4. A note in docs/accessibility.md on choosing sequential vs diverging, and on why rainbow/jet ramps are rejected.

WORTH CONSIDERING ALONGSIDE
The same consumer's categorical palettes show the related gap: four group colours sat in an L* band of 44.7-51.4, so slate and purple were dE 12.5 apart with normal colour vision and 10.1 under protanopia, and under deuteranopia three of the four collapsed together. A `DiscretePalette` documented as colour-vision-safe, with lightness separation rather than hue rotation alone, would prevent that class of defect too. `DiscretePalette` currently just wraps a caller-supplied vector (Scales.scala:842-874).

Filed from the PLS Neuro consumer side; that repository's integration ticket is bd-01M21SP4NDN67JM5MMMZ5Q4WWK, which fixed the immediate sign contradiction locally by naming one convention in the application. The local fix does not remove the library gap that caused it.
set.title: Provide a diverging signed palette primitive with a neutral midpoint
